## The problem

Planning data lives in separate tabs for each ship, and combining it into one
view is a recurring weekly task. Port names are also spelled differently from
one source to another, which makes comparisons error-prone.

## What I did

- Wrote a Python script that reads every ship's tab, standardizes the columns
  and stacks them into one combined dataset.
- Added fuzzy matching to line up port names that are spelled differently, so
  the combined file can be checked against the itinerary system of record.
- Built it to run the same way every week, so the output is consistent and
  easy to repeat.

## Results

The script cut analysis time by 30% and gives the team one consistent
dataset to work from every week.

## What I learned

Real-world text is messy. A good automation script has to expect variations,
like abbreviations and spelling differences, instead of assuming every source
follows the same format.

*Details are kept general to protect company data.*
